messages:
aurora_support: Heads-up — our CI provider (Aurora CI) found a client_secret pattern leaked in a public workflow run for repo `aurora/redwood-integration`. We rotated creds but wanted to confirm impact for Redwood customers. DM'd a sanitized log snippet and a private artifact URL. Sorry for the noise.

sec_ops_bot: [automated] vendor-repo-scan detected potential secret pattern in public CI logs (severity: medium). Notified sec-team.

alex_w: @aurora_support thanks for the ping. Quick Qs: which client_id was exposed? prod/dev? timeline of when secret appeared and when rotated?

aurora_support: client_id: aurora-client-7f2b (we partially redacted in public). It appeared in a public GH Actions run on 2026-03-17 22:41 UTC. We rotated the client_secret at 2026-03-18 09:12 UTC and invalidated the old secret. The workflow accidentally printed an environment var; the repo was public. We do not see obvious exfil beyond the single run. Link DM'd.

maria_s: @aurora_support can you confirm if the old secret was used to call Redwood APIs? @jamal I'll start searching ingress logs. Also please provide the exact GH run URL and the raw log snippet (sanitized is fine).

jamal: Running queries now for client_id aurora-client-7f2b across the last 30 days. I'll check our API gateway logs, token introspection hits, and KMS decrypts. Will report if I see successful auths.

aurora_support: Pasted a sanitized snippet in the DM. Example line (sanitized):
```
2026-03-17T22:41:03Z | runner/1234 | export AURORA_SECRET=***redacted***
2026-03-17T22:41:05Z | runner/1234 | curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ingest -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***redacted***'
```
We also uploaded full run logs to the private S3 link we shared via DM.

alex_w: OK action list: 1) Rotate any Redwood-side API keys/credentials bound to that client_id if present, 2) Revoke any active grants/tokens referencing aurora-client-7f2b, 3) Check KMS envelope key usage and grant lists, 4) Request vendor to adopt short-lived OIDC tokens for CI integration. Assign @maria_s and @tess_liaison. ETA 4h for initial containment.

maria_s: Acknowledged. Creating emergency ticket: SEC-2026-041. I'll rotate RBAC roles scoped to the vendor integration, revoke all existing long-lived tokens for that client_id, and forward vendor audit logs into SIEM for deeper analysis.

tess_liaison: I've opened a vendor comms thread and requested the CI run metadata (commit sha, runner IPs, timestamps) plus an attestation that the old secret was not stored in any accessible artifact beyond the run. Asked them to provide signed statement for our records.

sec_ops_bot: [automated] queued job: revoke-vendor-tokens(aurora-client-7f2b).

jamal: Update: found 3 successful calls using aurora-client-7f2b in the last 48 hours — all to sandbox endpoints (non-prod) and from a single IP block associated with a known CI runner fleet. No KMS decrypt operations observed tied to that client_id. I've applied an IP block rule for that range and revoked the tokens. Uploading query results to SEC-2026-041.

aurora_support: Confirmed on our end: rotated, invalidated, and we are auditing other runs. We also enabled short-lived token issuance for GH Actions and will push a config change to never print env vars. We'll provide a formal post-incident note by EOD.

alex_w: Thanks team — good containment. Next steps (post-containment): 1) vendor onboarding policy update (require OIDC/workflow tokens, no long-lived client secrets), 2) require vendor CI audit log ingestion or signed attestations for incidents, 3) add vendor-service-account RBAC review every 30 days, 4) ensure KMS usage alerts for any vendor-related decrypts. @maria_s can you take the lead on policy changes?

maria_s: Yep. I'll put together a policy draft and a Jira epic to enforce OIDC for new integrations. Also plan to increase vendor integration audit retention to 90 days and enable structured audit forwarding to our SIEM.

tess_liaison: I'll coordinate follow-up comms with Aurora and capture their attestation in the vendor risk record.

ajmal? (typo corrected) jamal: Also recommending a short runbook snippet we can add to vendor onboarding: how to rotate client secrets, how to revoke, and required log retention. I'll draft it.

alex_w: Good. We'll run a post-incident review once we have the vendor attestation and our SIEM results. Closing immediate containment here — open SEC-2026-041 for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

aurora_support: Thanks Redwood team. Sorry this happened — appreciate the quick containment and clear steps. We'll share the signed statement once legal completes it.
